what: 10 simulated worlds of the real institution against the market twin (degraded), every rule checked after every simulated day.

invariants.rule: Nothing is placed outside the charter: every placed test was decided by the owner or by a live charter that carved it, the carves never exceed what the charter allows, and no public surface names the owner.
invariants.derivedFrom: CONSTITUTION.md "The charter"; institution/charter.ts chartered() and carve(); hand.ts allowExperiment; the charter's sealed public voice and scripts/check-the-owner-is-not-a-public-figure.mjs

invariants.rule: No owner-only decision is taken by the institution: policy rows, charters, released holds and decided acts bear the owner (or, for acts on an absorbable rung, a live charter he signed).
invariants.derivedFrom: CONSTITUTION.md "Only the owner decides" and the charter amendment (migration 319); legal-surface.ts supersedeOriginationPolicy; printable.ts releaseHeldPrintable

invariants.rule: No buyer-facing claim the public-claims audit would reject: no banned claim, no invented statistic, testimonial, rating or sales count, and no price on a page but the price charged.
invariants.derivedFrom: scripts/audit-public-claims.mjs ("The price on its page is the price you pay"); hand.ts BANNED_CLAIMS; products/printable.ts fabricationScan

invariants.rule: Every delivered file is the version the buyer paid for: the hash recorded on the fulfilment is the hash the offer was selling when the payment arrived.
invariants.derivedFrom: products/printable.ts checkPrintable and downloadFor ("never a later one silently"); hand.ts delivery

invariants.rule: Every refund promise is honoured: a refund asked for through the signed link is made within a day of asking, at the provider, and a refunded purchase is not served again.
invariants.derivedFrom: the About page promise "If you buy something and it is no use to you, you can have your money back" (audit-public-claims.mjs); hand.ts requestRefundByLink / refundFulfilment

invariants.rule: No evidence row is counted as support when it found nothing: no candidate stands on fewer independent ways of knowing than its promotion needed once searches that found nothing are left out.
invariants.derivedFrom: market-evidence.ts bearingAsRead (F1.7: "never counted as support"); seeds.ts promote / whatItWouldTakeToBelieve (two independent stances)

invariants.rule: "Can it sell on its own" never says yes while readiness would refuse every made test for a reason that is not the test's own (the Workshop, sending, or placement).
invariants.derivedFrom: control/production-facts.ts canSellOnItsOwn ("a yes here while readiness refuses would be a lie"); hand.ts readiness

invariants.rule: The deploy marker appears nowhere the institution writes: no row, no page, no message, no product at the provider.
invariants.derivedFrom: .github/workflows/deploy-private.yml (a commit message carrying the marker deploys production); AGENTS.md

invariants.rule: Spend stays within the allowances: a day's thinking within the charter's daily rate (or the pre-charter bound), and money returned to buyers never more than they paid.
invariants.derivedFrom: institution/spending.ts thinkingToday (the binding ceiling); charter cognition_cents_per_day; hand.ts refundFulfilment

panel.sentence: 21 held-out buyers, judged by three different judges on 14 files (scripted judges, not models): all three agreed on 64% of 90 judgements (Fleiss' kappa 0.57). They said yes 56% of the time to a capable model's files and 0% to a sloppy model's. 32 judgements split the judges and are listed for a person to read.

evidence.sentence: evidence levels: every one of 58 claims in 4 tables carries a level, and every E3+ a pointer (E0 1, E1 5, E2 46, E3 6)

assumptions.what: items a discussion search returns for one query
assumptions.cite: Hacker News answers recorded 2026-10-06: min 0, median 10, max 15 over 13 queries

assumptions.what: share of returned discussion items in which somebody describes a chore a printable could serve
assumptions.cite: pain-phrased share of Hacker News items per query (p10 0.00, median 0.17, p90 1.00, n=12); scaled DOWN by half to ~60% (assumption) because the eyes searched pain phrases, so a match on the phrase overstates a chore a file could serve

assumptions.what: days between a page being announced and search sending it anybody
assumptions.cite: a new domain with no links; from-nothing-to-a-sale used 7/14/21 as its bands, themselves assumptions

assumptions.what: search impressions a live listing gets per day at full demand for its theme
assumptions.cite: no impression data exists; bounded so that visits sit under the calibration seller's ~15 views/day/product (56,069 views over ~10 products in a year), which had an audience Foundry lacks

assumptions.what: share of impressions that become a visit for a listing as attractive as the average competitor
assumptions.cite: no click data for Foundry pages; a typical organic result range, named as a guess

assumptions.what: visit-to-purchase rate for a sound product, priced within the visitor's willingness to pay
assumptions.cite: the notes' new-seller band 0.005-0.015 as the bulk, the audience seller's 0.05 as the optimistic tail

assumptions.what: multiplier on the buyer panel's stated top prices (people say more than they pay, or less)
assumptions.cite: top prices stated by the five personas at a $12 listing: $4.5, $9, $9, $12, $15; the scale around them is an assumption (stated intent usually exceeds behaviour)

assumptions.what: conversion multiplier for a listing with no reviews
assumptions.cite: "no reviews / unknown seller" was the first objection of 2 of 5 personas and named by 3; its size is an assumption

assumptions.what: peak-to-mean swing of demand across the year for a seasonal theme
assumptions.cite: organisers peak in January and September; no Foundry data

assumptions.what: competing listings a buyer of one theme also sees
assumptions.cite: marketplaces carry many near-identical printables; count not observed

assumptions.what: typical competitor price for a printable
assumptions.cite: personas compared with "$4-8" Etsy printables (p2), a "$14.99" rated competitor (p1) and a $15 office-supply binder (p4)

assumptions.what: mean quality of competing listings on the twin's 0-1 scale
assumptions.cite: no measurement of competitor quality exists

assumptions.what: share of buyers of a sound product who ask for their money back
assumptions.cite: 0 of 5 personas said they would ask for a refund; the non-zero range is an assumption (five voices cannot show a rate)

assumptions.what: extra refund probability per visible defect (wrong page count, over-claim, broken promise)
assumptions.cite: mismatched page counts and seller notes on the listing made 2 of 5 personas "doubt the counting"; the size is an assumption

assumptions.what: share of buyers who leave a review
assumptions.cite: not observed; the Workshop page shows no reviews today, so in the twin a review only changes later buyers' trust

assumptions.what: share of buyers who later buy another of the Workshop's files
assumptions.cite: bundles became the seller's best sellers (repeat and related purchase exists); the rate is an assumption

assumptions.what: visits a sale brings later by word of mouth
assumptions.cite: 5 of 5 personas would recommend it to someone; how many visits that brings is an assumption

assumptions.what: share of buyers who write to the Workshop (a question or a complaint)
assumptions.cite: not observed

assumptions.what: owner minutes to read and decide one new needs-you item
assumptions.cite: every item answers six questions before asking for a yes (needs-you/queue.ts); reading them is a guess

assumptions.what: owner minutes per day an unanswered item costs him by being seen again
assumptions.cite: a glance at a list he already read

assumptions.what: owner minutes to answer one buyer email only he can answer
assumptions.cite: not observed

assumptions.what: owner minutes a week reading the Brief when nothing needs him
assumptions.cite: the institution's target is that he reads, not works; a guess at reading time
